The story is an original piece of writing that avoids clichés in both its prose and its plot. Rather than relying on melodramatic tropes about infidelity, dramatic breakups, or lingering romantic obsession with an ex-spouse, the narrative explores the quieter, more nuanced psychological territory of chronic hesitation and emotional inertia. The central metaphor—a recurring dream about paying for an unused flat with an ex-wife—is unique and freshly rendered, as are the dry, understated observations and dialogue between the characters (e.g., "a refrigerator hummed as though nobody had told it the household was over," or "They had simply become proficient at disappointing one another").
